title: Chapter 6
content:
The overwhelming perfume of red roses hung heavy in the air, but every nerve in Jakyeong’s body was dialed in on the man sitting beside him.

Why did Kang Il-hyun stroke my hand like that? What was he checking for?

Yet for the entire drive, Il-hyun simply stared out the window, offering no explanation and making no further small talk.

The sedan glided across the Incheon Bridge in suffocating silence. Outside, a dense, milky haze hung over the sea—whether it was ocean fog or heavy smog, Jakyeong couldn't tell. Beyond the endless span of the bridge, the city skyline began to take shape. It had been nearly five years since he last set foot in Korea.

Whenever he returned to Korean soil, ghosts of his past inevitably resurfaced. It wasn't sorrow or heartbreak he felt—just a numb, detached curiosity. He used to indulge in the occasional fantasy of what life might have been like if his parents had lived, but deep down, he knew better. A alternate timeline wouldn't have saved him.

He would have been beaten to death, starved in a gutter, or—if he was exceptionally lucky—grown up to be just another junkie on the corner.

"Have you been back to Korea before?"

Il-hyun’s voice broke the silence, tossed out casually as he kept his eyes on the passing scenery.

Jakyeong offered a faint, polite nod. His mission here was clear: charm his way into this man's inner circle and pinpoint the exact location of his personal safe. Securing the safe was far trickier than taking a life. Offing Kang Il-hyun? He could do that right now in the back of this car if he wanted to.

"A few times with my mother," Jakyeong replied smoothly. "To visit my grandfather."

"I see. Your Korean is remarkably fluent."

"Thank you, Director Kang."

"You know, we actually met once before in Tokyo," Il-hyun added idly. "Do you remember?"

Jakyeong’s pulse spiked. What?

According to his intel, the real Jang Yi-an was a ghost who practically lived under house arrest, shielded from the public eye. Cold sweat pooled in Jakyeong’s palms as internal alarm bells rang in his head. Fighting to keep his composure, he maintained a placid, innocent expression.

"Is that so? I'm afraid... I don't recall."

"It was just a brief moment. You couldn't have been more than four or five."

Thank God. So they hadn't met as adults.

"You threw a full-blown tantrum, clenching my pant leg and sobbing hysterically."

"I... did?"

"It was our very first meeting, and to this day, I have no idea why you were crying."

"Haha..." Jakyeong let out a soft, awkward laugh. "I must have been quite a handful."

"You were. So I hit you. You bled all over your nose, and my father gave me a earful for it."

The air inside the luxury vehicle turned arctic in an instant. Judging by Il-hyun's utterly flat expression, the man seemed genuinely annoyed he hadn't hit the kid harder.

Jakyeong sat frozen, caught completely off guard. Was he supposed to apologize for a childhood beating he didn't remember? Say he was sorry for being a nuisance as a toddler? Or was this just Il-hyun's sick idea of a joke?

Before Jakyeong could figure out how to navigate the moment, Il-hyun’s phone rang. Saved by the bell. Jakyeong silently prayed the man would stay on the line for the rest of the drive and leave him alone.

"Speak," Il-hyun commanded into the receiver.

His prayer went unanswered.

"Understood," Il-hyun said, ending the call after a single phrase. He immediately called out to the driver. "Tae-soo. Turn us around. We're going to the factory."

"Yes, sir." Without a moment's hesitation, Tae-soo signaled, executed a sharp U-turn, and headed back the way they came.

Factory? Is there a plant nearby?

"It seems we'll be arriving home a bit late," Il-hyun said, turning back to Jakyeong. "Something urgent came up that requires my attention."

Great. More time trapped in this rolling coffin with you.

Jakyeong forced a sweet, accommodating smile. "Please, don't worry about it. And feel free to drop the formal speech with me, Director Kang. I'm much younger than you anyway. I'd like to think of you as an older brother."

Il-hyun shut him down instantly. "I'd rather not."

"Ah... as you wish, then."

Jakyeong turned his head toward the window, the fake smile melting off his face. Bastard. Prickly as a hedgehog. He cursed the man out in his head, already plotting how to break through that icy exterior.

Soon, the sedan veered off the main highway, taking a sharp turn onto a secluded side road heading in the opposite direction.

As he watched the passing landscape, a faint, rhythmic tapping echoed beside him. Tap. Tap. Tap.

Il-hyun was drumming his fingers against the glass with a bored expression—a strangely childish habit that clashed wildly with his cold, intimidating presence.

As they drove further, the city faded. Buildings and traffic gave way to open fields and dense brush. The occasional roadside diner vanished entirely. Eventually, the smooth asphalt turned into a rough, unpaved dirt trail. Even with the luxury sedan’s top-tier suspension, the chassis jostled softly over the ruts.

Outside, towering weeds stood as tall as a man—a classic horror movie backdrop. It looked like the kind of place a masked killer would emerge from, brandishing a rusty scythe.

After another thirty minutes of navigating the wasteland, the car slowed down. In the distance, an abandoned warehouse came into view.

Constructed from rusted shipping containers, calling it a "factory" was a generous overstatement. A crowd of men clad in tailored black suits stood gathered outside the entrance. Broad-shouldered and imposing, an unmistakable aura of violence radiated from them even from a distance.

The sedan pulled to a stop a short distance away. Almost in unison, Il-hyun and Tae-soo unbuckled their seatbelts.

"Stay in the car, Yi-an," Il-hyun instructed smoothly.

Jakyeong gave a docile nod. "Of course. Take your time."

Il-hyun and Tae-soo stepped out and strode toward the warehouse. From the calm atmosphere, it didn't look like a turf war was breaking out. Upon seeing Il-hyun, the mob of men parted with military precision.

Jakyeong’s eyes widened slightly.

Through the opening in the crowd, he spotted a man kneeling in the dirt. His face was a pulp of blood and bruises. Curious, Jakyeong leaned forward, peering through the tinted glass. The driver glanced at him through the rearview mirror, but Jakyeong didn't bother hiding his interest.

As Il-hyun approached, the men bowed in unison at a ninety-degree angle. The bloodied man on his knees, hands bound tightly behind his back, began kowtowing frantically, his forehead smashing against the gravel. Though no sound carried into the car, his posture screamed desperate begging for his life.

Il-hyun, however, had zero interest in dialogue.

In a single, fluid motion, he snatched a handgun from the holster of a guard standing nearby and raised it. Before Jakyeong could even process the move—BANG!

The gunshot echoed clearly inside the luxury cabin. The back of the kneeling man's skull burst open, and he collapsed onto his side like a sack of bricks.

BANG! BANG! BANG!

Il-hyun put three more rounds cleanly into the man's chest. Without missing a beat, he handed the gun back to its owner and pulled out a cigarette. With a lazy flick of his hand, a guard stepped forward, drew a heavy butcher knife from his jacket, and knelt over the fresh corpse to carve something out.

Tossing his half-finished cigarette onto the body, Il-hyun turned and walked back to the car.

Jakyeong’s lips pressed into a tight, flat line, his eyes tracking Il-hyun's every step. He’s done this a thousand times. The draw was effortless, the aim was dead center on the vitals, and there wasn't a fraction of a second's hesitation.

Jakyeong quickly straightened his posture, putting on his best oblivious-innocent mask.

The rear door opened, and Il-hyun slid back inside. A heavy cocktail of acrid cordite and fresh tobacco smoke flooded the interior.

"My apologies," Il-hyun said smoothly, his tone as casual as if he’d just been delayed by a quick bathroom break. "It was pressing business. Couldn't be rescheduled."

Jakyeong’s mind raced. How should a sheltered rich kid react to seeing someone executed in front of him?

Though raised in the underworld, the real Jang Yi-an had been coddled under his grandfather’s wing like a delicate greenhouse flower. How was a timid, ordinary twenty-one-year-old supposed to act right now?

While searching for the right line, Jakyeong noticed a tiny streak of blood spattered across Il-hyun’s right cheek.

"Why are you staring at me like that?" Il-hyun asked.

"There's... blood on your face."

Il-hyun raised a hand, lazily wiping his jaw with his palm, only spreading it slightly.

Jakyeong hesitated, then reached into his trousers and pulled out a neatly folded handkerchief. Wang Han had forced him to pack it before he left for Korea, insisting that a pampered young master always carried a handkerchief. Jakyeong had mocked him at the time, but who would have thought it would actually come in handy? Leave it to a guy raised on Confucian values to occasionally make a brilliant call.

Leaning over, Jakyeong gently dabbed the blood off Il-hyun’s cheek.

Il-hyun’s dark eyes locked onto Jakyeong's, watching him intently.

Folding the stained cloth back up, Jakyeong tucked it away and offered the most polite, innocent smile he could muster. "There. All clean now."

He turned his gaze back toward the windshield. Outside, Il-hyun’s men were hoisting a steel oil drum containing the corpse onto the back of a flatbed truck. Jakyeong already knew where that drum was headed—somewhere deep enough that no one would ever find it. A ditch in the woods, or the bottom of the ocean. Just like his own parents.

At least this guy was lucky enough to be dead before they dumped him, Jakyeong thought grimly. My parents were thrown in alive.

Feeling an intense glare burning into his cheek, Jakyeong turned back around.

Il-hyun was still staring at him. His gaze was so sharp and relentless it felt like a physical prickle against Jakyeong’s skin. The car remained parked, and the mounting tension was becoming unbearable.

"Is there... something else on my face, Director Kang?"

Il-hyun’s eyes slowly drifted downward, scanning Jakyeong’s body. A cold wave of tension washed over Jakyeong. He had intentionally worn an oversized shirt and baggy pants to hide his muscular build, but had the bastard noticed something anyway?

Il-hyun’s eyes finally stopped at the bouquet of red roses resting on Jakyeong's lap.

"It seems I made an excellent choice," Il-hyun murmured softly.

"Pardon?"

"They suit you. The red roses."

What the hell is this bastard talking about?

Before Jakyeong could even process the nauseating line, Il-hyun leaned back into his leather seat as if nothing had happened, gazing out the front windshield.

Jakyeong clamped his jaw shut, fighting with everything he had to keep his face from twisting into a grimace.

An oppressive silence fell over the car once more. Fuck's sake. Would it kill you to turn on the radio?

The sedan pulled away, navigating back through the sea of towering weeds. The wild brush that had felt harmless on the way in now felt identical to the man sitting beside him—dense, untamed, and completely impossible to see through.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

Incheon Bridge (인천대교): A massive 21.3 km cable-stayed bridge connecting Incheon International Airport on Yeongjong Island to the mainland city of Incheon.
Formality Drop (말을 놓다): Jakyeong offers Il-hyun permission to drop jondetmal (formal/polite speech) and speak casually (banmal), signaling closeness. Il-hyun's blunt rejection ("I'd rather not") is an explicit social snub, establishing a strict hierarchy and boundary between them.
